discovery: Discovery of quantum error correction and topological codes, establishing that fragile quantum information can be protected and processed fault-tolerantly
subfield: Quantum information physics / quantum error correction
motivation: Before 1995, many physicists believed decoherence made large-scale quantum coherent machines impossible: the no-cloning theorem and continuous errors seemed to forbid redundancy. Shor (1995) and Steane (1996) independently discovered that quantum information can be encoded in entangled states of many particles so that errors are detected and corrected without measuring the encoded state. Kitaev (1997) showed that information stored in topologically ordered states, the toric and surface codes, is protected by locality, giving a physically natural route to fault tolerance with high thresholds. These ideas created a new branch of physics linking many-body entanglement, topological order and measurement. They now guide experiments on every major platform: in 2023-2025, superconducting and atomic processors showed logical error rates falling below threshold as code size grows, and bosonic codes surpassed break-even. This is a conceptual discovery with deep physical content and profound technological consequence.
